bank.keyText: The neuron can no longer fire action potentials

The resting potential immediately rises to 0 mV

answer.text: The neuron can no longer fire action potentials
answer.line: Voltage-gated Na+ channels carry the upstroke. Block them and no spike can start, though the resting potential stays put.

steps: Name the channel's job. Voltage-gated Na+ channels open at threshold and let Na+ rush in: that is the upstroke.
Block them and no Na+ rushes in. No upstroke, no action potential.
The resting potential stays near normal. The K+ leak channels and the Na+/K+ pump that set it are untouched.

choices.text: Neurotransmitter release increases at the terminal
choices.note: No action potential reaches the terminal, so release falls, not rises.

choices.text: The resting potential immediately rises to 0 mV
choices.note: The resting potential belongs to the K+ leak channels and the pump, which the toxin leaves alone. Rest stays near -70 mV.

choices.text: The neuron fires action potentials continuously
choices.note: Continuous firing is what a toxin that holds Na+ channels open would do. This one blocks them.

choices.text: Repolarization fails, so the membrane stays positive
choices.note: Repolarization is the job of the K+ channels, and here it never gets the chance. The spike never starts, so the membrane never goes positive.

choices.text: The neuron can no longer fire action potentials
choices.note: No Na+ entry, no upstroke, no spike.

lockIt: Na+ in makes the upstroke; K+ out brings it down. Block the Na+ channels and nothing fires.

visual.reuse: new plot; values as in the Action Potential lab of tools/bio/bio-physiology.html (rest -70 mV, threshold -55 mV, peak +30 mV)
visual.alt: Two membrane potential traces. The normal neuron rests at -70 mV, reaches the -55 mV threshold, shoots up to +30 mV as Na+ flows in, and falls back as K+ flows out. With tetrodotoxin, outlined as the answer, the same stimulus gives only a small bump with no upstroke, and rest stays near -70 mV.
visual.caption: Compare the two traces at threshold: one takes off, the blocked one sags back to rest.
